SPEC:
order(deps) takes a dict mapping each node (a string) to the list of nodes it depends on. It returns a list containing every node mentioned anywhere, in which each node comes after all of its dependencies. When several nodes are ready at the same time the smallest string goes first, and readiness is re-evaluated after every pick. A dependency cycle, including a node that depends on itself, raises CycleError, which mod.py defines. Examples are Python. order({'b': ['a'], 'c': ['b']}) is ['a', 'b', 'c']. order({'c': ['a'], 'b': ['a']}) is ['a', 'b', 'c']. order({'x': ['y']}) is ['y', 'x']. order({'b': ['a'], 'c': [], 'a': []}) is ['a', 'b', 'c']. order({'a': ['b'], 'b': ['a']}) raises CycleError.
